headline.text: The FDA olopatadine nasal spray label describes additional impairment with alcohol.

reported.text: The warning concerns olopatadine nasal spray and possible additional reductions in alertness and CNS performance.

claims.text: The FDA olopatadine nasal spray label says alcohol may further reduce alertness and impair CNS performance.
claims.quote: Concurrent use of olopatadine hydrochloride nasal spray with alcohol or other central nervous system depressants should be avoided because additional reductions in alertness and additional impairment of central nervous system performance may occur.
claims.judgeRationale: The olopatadine nasal spray label states additional reductions in alertness and CNS performance may occur with alcohol.

pharmacistQuestions.text: The label describes this interaction, but there seem to be no human studies of it. How is it usually handled for someone like me?
Do any of my other medicines or products, like cough syrup or mouthwash, contain alcohol?
Does my dose, or the time between taking Olopatadine and drinking alcohol, change how much this matters?

gaps.text: The packet contains no human interaction study of this combination.
searched: (ethanol[tiab] OR alcohol[tiab]) AND "olopatadine"[tiab] AND (interaction OR coadministration)
